answer: The vein is what a clone cannot copy. A seat is one cut face on a registered marble bench: the applicant files bench coordinates, a wire-saw licence and a flatbed scan of the face. Veins run unique to a block, so the node keeps each scan and refuses a second seat matching it inside tolerance. Quarterly a fresh face is scanned, an air knife clearing the zephyr of dust, and the slab rides a river barge on one ticket. Per clone: licence 12,000 dollars, saw 40,000, extraction 3,500, rig 1,800, so fifty seats pass 2.8 million before a slab floats. A river bends alike twice; its banks never do.
